children: , the software and cloud giant, put a new label on its massive AI spending push Wednesday, with shares priced at $497.515. Management calls the key measure useful yieldhow many valuable tokens Microsoft can produce from every dollar and watt. That metric matters when quarterly capital spending is already 2.1 times free cash flow.

The numbers are enormous. Fiscal fourth-quarter capital expenditure hit $41 billion, including $5.6 billion in finance leases. Operating cash flow reached $55.4 billion, yet free cash flow landed at just $19.6 billion. Microsoft Cloud delivered $59.3 billion in revenue, putting infrastructure spending at roughly 69% of quarterly cloud sales.

Now comes the hard part: proving those billions can generate strong returns before chips age and power bottlenecks tighten. The picture offers one bullish signalMicrosoft's $497.515 share price sits 14.39% below its $581.15 GF Value estimate. But the valuation gap alone is not enough. Useful yield only becomes useful to investors when Microsoft provides a clear baseline, measurable targets and consistent progress.

title: Microsoft's $41 Billion AI Spending Push Gets a New Investor Scorecard
